rounds.text: Vardhman Polytex is currently undergoing a significant operational inflection point, evidenced by a massive 83% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months [E15]. This recent performance represents a sharp departure from historical stagnation, as confirmed by the 61% year-over-year sales increase [E57] and profit growth exceeding 20% [E60]. The market has failed to price in this momentum, as the stock trades at a P/E of 41.56x, which is a discount to the sector benchmark of 48.76x [E5]. Furthermore, the company is beginning to outperform expectations, with profit growth exceeding one-year price growth by 102% [E48]. Conceded: the company has struggled with long-term sales growth [E12, E13, E52], poor returns on assets [E7], and a lack of dividend payments [E3]. Despite these historical headwinds, the current acceleration in top-line and bottom-line growth suggests the business is fundamentally changing its trajectory [E15, E60].

Conceded: trailing twelve months compounded sales growth reached 83% [E15]. However, this short-term surge sits atop a decade of structural stagnation, evidenced by a 10-year compounded sales growth of just 1% and a 5-year growth of 0% [E12, E13]. The bull highlights a P/E discount [E5], but ignores the profound balance sheet distress indicated by a negative book value and a negative price-to-book ratio of -0.52x [E1]. Furthermore, the business destroys capital rather than compounding it, carrying a dismal return on assets of -9.24% that drastically underperforms the sector benchmark of -4.06% [E7], alongside an absolute zero return on equity [E8]. Compounded share price growth of -30% over the past year [E23] directly refutes the idea that the market is missing a turnaround, especially when current signals explicitly flag decelerating earnings growth [E61].
